To find the stationary points of an equation y = f(x), first, find the first derivative of the function, f'(x). Then, set the first derivative equal to zero and solve for x. These values of x are the critical points. Next, find the second derivative of the function, f''(x). Finally, evaluate the second derivative at each critical point. If f''(x) is positive, the function has a local minimum at that point. If f''(x) is negative, the function has a local maximum at that point. If f''(x) is zero, the test is inconclusive and further analysis is needed.
